Since \(\overrightarrow{OA}=2\overrightarrow{OB}\), we have
\[
2\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OA}=2(\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB}).
\]
Thus the condition becomes
\[
2|\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB}|^2=0,
\]
so \(\overrightarrow{OC}=\overrightarrow{OB}=(0,2)\).

Now minimize
\[
\left|\overrightarrow{OB}-\frac14 t\overrightarrow{OA}-\frac12[\ln(-t)-1]\overrightarrow{OB}\right|.
\]
Since \(\overrightarrow{OA}=(0,4)\), \(\overrightarrow{OB}=(0,2)\),
\[
\frac14 t\overrightarrow{OA}=(0,t),\qquad \frac12[\ln(-t)-1]\overrightarrow{OB}=(0,\ln(-t)-1).
\]
So the distance is
\[
|2-t-(\ln(-t)-1)|=|3-t-\ln(-t)|.
\]
Let \(s=-t>0\). Then
\[
|3-t-\ln(-t)|=|3+s-\ln s|.
\]
The function \(3+s-\ln s\) has minimum at \(s=1\), with value \(4\), and is positive. Therefore the minimum is
\[
\boxed{4}.
\]
